question: What is the difference between `malloc()` and `new`?

scenes.sub: One hands you bytes. The other hands you an object.
scenes.say: malloc versus new. Both get memory from the heap. But only one of them gives you a real object.

scenes.head: Bytes versus a constructed object
scenes.say: malloc is a C function. It only hands you raw bytes of the size you ask for. No constructor runs, so the string inside a was never built. Using a arrow name is undefined behavior. new does two things. It allocates memory, and then it runs the constructor. So b points to a fully built Player, with its name set to hero.

scenes.head: Size, type, and failure
scenes.say: More differences. malloc returns void star, so C plus plus needs a cast, and you count the bytes yourself. new knows the type, so it computes the size and returns the right pointer type. On failure, malloc returns null. new throws s t d colon colon bad alloc instead, unless you ask for the no throw version. And each has its own partner: malloc with free, new with delete. Never mix them.

scenes.head: Side by side
scenes.say: malloc is a library function, new is an operator, which a class can even overload. Constructor: only new runs it. Size: bytes versus the type. Return type: void star versus a typed pointer. On failure: null versus an exception. Release: free versus delete. And resizing: malloc has realloc. With new, you allocate a new block and move the elements, which is exactly what vector does for you.

lines: malloc: raw bytes, no constructor, returns void*, NULL on failure.
new: allocates and constructs, typed pointer, throws std::bad_alloc.
Pair malloc/free and new/delete. In C++, prefer new (or better, make_unique).
scenes.say: malloc gives raw bytes, with no constructor, and returns null on failure. new allocates and constructs, returns a typed pointer, and throws on failure. Never mix the pairs. And in modern C plus plus, prefer make unique over either one.
